newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse edged up, consolidation extended.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse edged up, consolidation extended.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended Friday on a higher note guided by Dow Jones gains, but failed to keep up with European bourses as the index extended its consolidation and investors sold shares with high gains.
"We are living in a consolidation period so I see no reason for any falls in the index except if some big move in interest rate sentiment in Europe occurs, which is unlikely," a dealer said.
The blue-chip Bel-20 index closed up 1.66 points or 0.09 percent higher at 1,865.21 from Thursday's 1,863.55 close.
Dealers expected the market to push up after consolidation, possibly beyond the 1,900 level by the end of the year.
One dealer said that much cash would come onto the market at the end of the year, with pension funds and life insurances getting more money, giving the index plenty of opportunity to rise.
Trade was slow in the early session but picked up during afternoon trade once the Dow Jones opened firm.
The market was also encouraged by the improvement in the National of Bank of Belgium's leading economic indicator which showed retail trade and industry growing.

Investors shrugged off political uncertainty surrounding the Belgian government, with dealers saying the sentiment was that the government could weather the sex allegations involving Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo.
Di Rupo strongly denies the allegations against him.
One dealer forecast pharmaceutical firm UCB to climb in coming weeks, encouraged by increased demand for its products and good prospects in the Japanese market.
It rose 0.4 percent to close at 76,150 francs.
Non-ferrous metals company Union Miniere ended unchanged from Thursday's close at 2,150 francs.
One dealer said interest in the stock had been renewed as investors shopped around for shares in companies that had lagged the recent index rises.
Elsewhere among financials steel maker Cockerill climbed 1.67 percent to 122 francs, with dealers attributing it down to technical corrections after having faced weeks of price falls.
Cockerill is expected to be replaced on the Bel-20 index by electronics firm Barco which ended up 60 francs at 5,470 francs.
